transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Lately I can’t seem to focus on my analyses at work—my mind keeps going blank even when I’m staring right at the spreadsheets. It's making it incredibly difficult to do my job, and I'm becoming really alarmed by how much it's affecting my performance.
Has this difficulty with focus and concentration been a lifelong struggle for you, or did these symptoms start relatively recently in response to a specific event or stressor?

No, this hasn't been a lifelong struggle for me. It actually started about fifteen months ago when I got promoted into a much higher-visibility, high-stress role at work. Ever since then, it has been a constant battle that hasn't really let up.

Beyond your difficulty with concentration at work, have you been experiencing other persistent symptoms like low mood, loss of interest in activities, or feelings of worthlessness for most of the day, nearly every day?

No, I wouldn't say I feel a low mood or worthlessness. I have stopped going to my running club and seeing friends, but it's not because I've lost interest—I just feel too anxious, wired, and constantly overwhelmed by work to actually show up and enjoy myself.

Besides your work-related anxiety, do you find that you feel excessively worried about a variety of other topics—such as your health, finances, or family safety—most days, or is your anxiety strictly centered around your performance at work?

It's definitely not just work, though that is a major focus. My mind is constantly spinning about all sorts of things, even minor details like whether I remembered to lock my apartment door. Once those "what if" thoughts start, they quickly snowball from one worst-case scenario to another, and I just can't seem to turn them off and relax.
Do you often experience physical symptoms like muscle tension, restlessness, or feeling easily fatigued alongside these persistent worries?

Yes, absolutely. I feel constantly exhausted, like I'm dragging my body through molasses even on weekends when I try to sleep in. My body is always incredibly tense and wired, and I never seem to feel truly at ease.
